case_title: Ohan Singh v. State of Haryana
neutral_facts: The prosecution case was that the deceased had a dispute with his brother over a residential house. On the date of the incident, the deceased, his wife, and his daughters were present in the house. The accused persons, including the brother of the deceased and the appellant, entered the house. The appellant was holding an iron rod and inflicted a blow on the head of the deceased. The brother of the deceased gave a lathi blow on other parts of the body of the deceased. Other accused also inflicted lathi blows on the deceased's back. Injuries were also inflicted on the deceased's wife. The accused persons then ran away. The injured were taken to the hospital. The Head Constable recorded the statement of the deceased, which was later treated as a dying declaration. The deceased died in the hospital after a few days. The case was converted into one under Section 302 IPC. The trial court found that the head injury attributed to the appellant was sufficient to cause the death of the deceased and convicted the appellant under Sections 148, 149, 323, 506, 452, and 302 IPC. The High Court refused to interfere with the trial court's order.
